record.original_question: If two division algebras have the same splitting fields inside a specified class of field extensions, for example finite extensions or extensions of transcendence degree at most one, must they generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.3. Determine whether two division algebras that have the same splitting fields in a given class (say finite, or of transcendence degree at most one), necessarily generate the same subgroup in the Brauer group.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K be a field and let Br(K) denote its Brauer group. For a central simple K-algebra A, a field extension L/K is called a splitting field of A if A⊗_K L is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over L. Fix a class C of field extensions of K (for example, the class of finite-dimensional extensions of K, or the class of extensions of transcendence degree at most one over K).

Suppose D₁ and D₂ are finite-dimensional central division algebras over K with the property that, for every L/K in the class C, L splits D₁ if and only if L splits D₂. Determine whether [D₁] and [D₂] must generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(K); that is, whether ⟨[D₁]⟩ = ⟨[D₂]⟩ in Br(K).
artifact.status_search_result: The question (a "genus"-type problem for division algebras restricted to a class of splitting fields) appears to remain open in general. Recent work, including a 2024 preprint constructing infinite families of division algebras sharing all finite splitting fields and all splitting fields of transcendence degree at most one, indicates that the answer can fail in some settings, but the precise question of whether shared splitting fields in such restricted classes force the algebras to generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group is not fully resolved; in particular the quaternion case over finitely generated fields remains open.

status_evidence.title: Genus of division algebras over fields with infinite transcendence degree
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of infinite collections of division algebras sharing all finite splitting fields and splitting fields of transcendence degree at most one.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work shows the restricted-splitting-field problem behaves nontrivially; resolution in full generality is not established.

status_evidence.title: Division algebras with the same maximal subfields (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the genus of a division algebra and notes open cases including quaternion algebras over finitely generated fields.
status_evidence.claim: The genus problem (closely related formulation) is partially solved with several open cases.
